body.statement: Under the Markov switchback, the certified integer window \(b_T=\lceil T^{1/(2\beta+1)}\rceil\) balances exposure variance of order \(b_T/T\) with squared replacement error of order \(b_T^{-2\beta}\). If one experimental period represents \(d\) units of clock time, the corresponding operational assignment window is \(d b_T\), while the retained homogeneous-history exposure length is \(b_T+1\) periods.
body.justification: This inherited supporting proposition expresses the audited design scale in the window language used by deployed switchback systems.
body.gap: The power-law window is an operational restatement of the banked oracle scale, informed by Xiong, Chin, and Taylor's modeled cadence components; it is not a separate novelty claim.
body.consumer: Marketplace teams can map an elicited decay index and experiment horizon to a pre-registered switchback window without claiming unknown-index adaptation.
body.proof_tex:
The certificate in \(\mathrm{lem{:}markov\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}audit}\) is the square of the sum of a standard-deviation term proportional to \((b/T)^{1/2}\) and a deterministic replacement term proportional to \((b+1)^{-\beta}\).  Thus its two squared contributions have orders \(b/T\) and \((b+1)^{-2\beta}\), respectively.  With \(x=T^{1/(2\beta+1)}\) and \(b_T=\lceil x\rceil\), one has \(x\le b_T\le x+1\le2x\), and hence
\[
 \frac{b_T}{T}\asymp T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)},
 \qquad
 (b_T+1)^{-2\beta}\asymp T^{-2\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
This proves the asserted balance of the two certified terms.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}markov\mbox{-}switchback}\), one period represents one transition opportunity; if one period lasts \(d\) clock-time units, a nominal window of \(b_T\) periods lasts \(db_T\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}truncated\mbox{-}ht}\), at a mature time \(t>b_T\) the event \(H_{t,b_T,a}=1\) retains the assignments at times \(t-b_T,\ldots,t\), namely \(b_T+1\) consecutive periods.  At the initial boundary it retains all \(t\) available periods through time \(t\), exactly as encoded by \(k_t=\min\{b_T,t-1\}\).
